independence_note: 'root-independent' is the fixed schema role required by the reviewed root code. No separate reviewer was staffed for this round: the owner instructed the executing session to proceed, so this is a same-session preparation review. Consequence: outputs of the run it authorizes are diagnostic evidence only and carry no acceptance credit.
evidence_checks: Diffed the new profile.py against the frozen original (sha 5c837adb...): six additive changes plus one narrowed predicate. Recorder caps moved from 64 sites / 6 frames to 32 sites / 10 frames (owner approved both). A _inside_import probe walks the live frame chain for a frozen importlib frame; _audit_site now also records the outermost non-machinery caller; WorkerAudit gained expected/expected_sites; audit_closeout gained expected/expected_sites/expected_truncated; write_expected_evidence plus one call site before the closed index; and the reader failure result now carries the guard message that stopped it, so a failed reconstruction names its own cause instead of returning a bare ValueError. The narrowed predicate: during a module body, socket.__new__ and a socket.bind to loopback with port zero are receipted as expected instead of denied. That pair is exactly one loopback family probe (create, bind an ephemeral port, close); the first acceptance run showed the probe reaching bind after creation was excused. Connect, send, listen, any non-loopback host and any non-zero port stay denied.

Diffed the new test_profile.py: two appended tests plus a fixture correction that now builds the END event in the executor order; the original 564 ids are retained and the package manifest carries 566 test ids.
Full fixed contracts in this package: exit 0, expected_count=actual_count=566, allowlist exact, dependencies (1462) unchanged, package files unchanged. Receipt kept under code/.
Root code copied from the reviewed entry with only two fixed package paths substituted (entry ROOT, controls BASE_MANIFEST) and the pinned profile digest updated; no other line differs.

Entry manifest rebuilt so that every bound input is an existing absolute path with a matching sha256, including the seven protected-process baseline and the E01 helper modules the native backend imports.

Rejected events are recorded as event name plus at most ten calling frames and the outermost non-machinery caller; argument values are never persisted, so the receipt cannot leak a command or a path argument. Excused import-time probes get their own receipt and never touch the clean flag.

Acceptance round 3 (run 08d462a2, exit 1) is the evidence for the bind half: with socket.__new__ excused the same import chain reached socket.bind at urllib3 util connection.py:127 and was refused there, both events carrying caller __init__.py:4. Round 4 (run 736eeb1e) refused the same bind because the predicate read args[0] while CPython raises socket.bind as (socket, address); a local probe recorded that shape and the predicate now scans every argument for the loopback ephemeral-port tuple. Across rounds 3 and 4 the product side wrote the 711-byte research.md with sha a7e7e590..., byte-identical to rounds 1 and 2.

Acceptance round 5 (run 89df0e1a, exit 1) moved the stop from the audit layer to the read-side byte comparison: the reader rebuilt the trace with the END data keys ordered tool, agent, success, latency, result, metadata while the pinned executor emits tool, success, latency, result, metadata, agent (openjarvis tools _stubs.py, publish of TOOL_CALL_END). Parsed values were equal, so every value-level guard passed and only the order-sensitive string comparison fired. The read-side projection now uses the executor order, and the three byte comparisons raise separate named messages so a later failure says which of catalogue, trace or attempts was off.
